title: Orbiting at the Max mesh with All sheets runs at 27 to 38 fps (base: 54 to 60)
detail: Turning the camera at the Max mesh (1920) with All sheets on, the user's case (sqrt then sin, Im), drops to about half the frame rate in every r3 run, desktop and phone. The base holds 54 to 60 fps on the same frames. Playing the deformation at Max is fine (54.8 to 60 fps), so the cost is in orbiting only. Likely cause, from the code: in sheetRefine, a moving frame over 256 cells keeps the refined sheets of the rest frame when the heights key has not changed (`if (move && ... (o.want||0) - 1 > 256) { if (o.rfFor !== o.key) o.rf = null; rfLater(); return; }`). Orbiting does not change the key, so every orbit frame draws the full rest refinement of every sheet, plus the edge pass and the facetW fragment stage. Playing changes the key each frame, so it draws the unrefined sheets. The default mesh (240) is fine: 60 fps orbiting and playing with All sheets, desktop and phone, 2 runs each. The round 3 tables never measured orbiting at Max with All sheets, so this was missed.
evidence: review-speed-runs/perf_max.json (base and r3 alternating B,T,T,B; camera yaw stepped every frame for 2.5 s, then play for 3 s, then 1.5 s after stop). Orbit, Max, All sheets: desktop r3 26.6 fps (p50 39, p95 44.1, max 167.8 ms) and 36.7 fps (p95 30.3, max 128.1); base 57.6 fps (p95 21.3) and 59.6 fps (p95 19.0). Phone 390x844: r3 32.6 fps (p95 38.8, max 155.7) and 37.9 fps (p95 28.9, max 116.8); base 58.0 fps (p95 24.1) and 54.0 fps (p95 26.5). Default mesh with All sheets: review-speed-runs/perf_default_all.json, r3 orbit 60 fps, p95 17.8 to 18.4.
fix: First find which pass costs the frame: time an orbit at Max with All sheets with the refined sheet draw, the edge pass and facetW each switched off in turn. Then limit the refined sheets at rest by what one frame can draw. For example, cap the rest budget by the sheet count (RF_REST_S / K), or cap the refined sub-cells drawn per frame. If the refined sheets cannot fit in a frame, treat camera motion over 256 cells like playing: draw the base sheets while the camera moves and refine again when it stops (rfLater already does this). Add an orbit-at-Max-with-All-sheets row to BUDGET60 in landscape_walls_cmd.js.

title: Cold opens: every r3 open has a second stall of 135 to 283 ms that the base does not have; first surface with All sheets is 130 to 260 ms slower
detail: Blocker 2 is not met with fresh, heavier formulas. Delaying first use until 900 ms after the link (settled) moves the second stall but does not remove it. With sheets off, the stall comes when the edge pass landEdgeS is first drawn, 0.9 to 1.1 s after the open. With All sheets, it comes when landSheetRF is first drawn, 1.37 to 1.53 s after the open. Each is a chain program, so a fresh formula compiles its Metal pipeline again. The base has neither program and no second stall. The first stall, at first draw, is also longer than the base's in every alternating pair (principal: 552 to 700 ms against 341 to 567; All sheets: 329 to 384 against 147 to 250). Machine noise was high (other agents' Chrome instances were running, and the base also stalled once in every run), but r3 is worse in all 8 alternating pairs.
evidence: review-speed-runs/cold_desktop.json: 8 + 8 opens at 1440x900, base and r3 alternating, every formula fresh (random constants). Formulas: log(z^3+K) sqrt(z^2-K), sqrt(z^5+K) cosh(z/4), log(z^4-Kz) sin(z/3), sqrt(z^3-K) tanh(z/2). Main-thread gaps over 100 ms: principal base 5 gaps (longest 567), r3 12 (longest 700); All sheets base 4 (longest 250), r3 9 (longest 384). Each r3 run has a second gap 1.70 to 1.90 s after the open (117 to 274 ms; the screenshot loop delays it); the base has a second gap in 1 of 8 runs. First surface with All sheets: r3 681, 710, 653, 646 ms against base 480, 449, 520, 466. review-speed-runs/plog.json (GLR._lwLog, no screenshots): sheets off, gap 966@283 ms with landEdgeS first used @966, and gap 1068@135 with landEdgeS @1068. All sheets: gap 1580@215 with landSheetRF @1530, and gap 1416@209 with landSheetRF @1366.
fix: Warm each new chain program by a draw that writes nothing, the same way rfWarmed warms the refinement's static programs, and do it before any frame depends on that program. Better, warm it right after its link, with KHR_parallel_shader_compile's completion as the trigger, in a frame that does no other first draws. Or fold the edge pass's and landSheetRF's work into programs the frame has already used, so a fresh formula pays for one first-draw stall, as the base does. Re-measure with fresh heavy formulas: the builder's sqrt(z^4+c) sin z list showed far fewer stalls than these.

title: Max mesh, principal surface, desktop: 92 to 252 ms hitches and BUDGET60 fails in 2 of 2 r3 runs (base 0 of 2)
detail: Playing and orbiting at Max with sheets off, desktop 1440x900: r3 had single long frames the base never had, and failed BUDGET60 in both of its runs. On the phone (390x844) the same case passed in both r3 runs (p95 17.7 to 19.0). The noise was high, but the base runs on either side were clean. The round 3 table (p95 18.6 to 19.1) did not catch the hitches.
evidence: review-speed-runs/perf_max.json, desktop Max, principal. r3 run 1: play 52.0 fps, p95 26.4, max 252.4 ms. r3 run 2: orbit 53.6 fps, p95 35.7, max 92.5; play 57.3 fps, p95 21.2, max 143.4. Base runs 1 and 2: orbit p95 18.0 and 18.2, play p95 18.5 and 18.3, max 19.7 or less.
fix: Log GLR._lwT (read and list times) and GLR._lwF (per-frame trace) for a Max principal play and match the long frames to their cause. Candidates: a forced level read (lvTake once LV_LATE has passed calls getBufferSubData while the GPU is still busy), a program's first draw, or rfLater's rest refinement starting in the middle of motion. If it is the late read, skip the read rather than block: let the levels stand one more frame instead of forcing the read at 60 ms.

title: More GPU texture memory held at rest: 56 MB after a play (base 8 MB), 23 MB after a sheets toggle (base 10 MB)
detail: WebGL create, delete and upload calls were wrapped to count live objects and the bytes uploaded. Mesh changes free memory correctly: Max then back to default takes r3 from 34.3 to 8.9 MB of textures, close to the base's 32 to 8.1. There is no growth over 10 formula changes, so no leak. But after toggling All sheets, r3 holds both surfaces' refinement objects: 25 textures, 22.6 MB, against the base's 5 and 10 MB. After playing the deformation and stopping it holds 32 textures, 56.1 MB, until the formula changes, when it falls back to 23.8 MB. One fence (sync) object also stays alive at rest after the Max visit, until the sheets are toggled. That is harmless, but it means lvTail is not always deleted when nothing is in flight. On a phone, about 45 MB of textures held while idle is worth trimming.
evidence: review-speed-runs/mem.json (default mesh 240, All sheets, user's case). base: rest 6 tex 9.8 MB; Max 32 MB; back 8.1 MB; sheets off/on 10 MB; after play 8.1 MB; after 10 formulas 8.1 MB. r3: rest 13 tex 10.6 MB; Max 34.3 MB with sync 1; back 8.9 MB with sync 1; sheets off 25 tex 22.6 MB; after play and stop 32 tex 56.1 MB; after 5 and 10 formulas 32 tex 23.8 to 23.9 MB. Buffers are about the same in both (32.1 against 32.6 MB after the Max visit).
fix: Free the motion-only textures (the moving path's level and list textures, and any per-T mesh entries kept after play) with rfFree when motion stops and the rest refinement has landed. Free the hidden surface's refinement objects when All sheets is toggled. In lvCollect, delete lvTail when no level read is in flight.

title: With All sheets on, the step cards' Landscapes appear about 3.1 s after the pane opens, and wait for as long as the pane keeps drawing
detail: card: true makes a card wait until the pane has not drawn for 1.5 s (landPane.t is reset on every pane frame), then until landTF and land have settled (900 ms after link). With All sheets, the pane never draws the principal programs, so the cards always take the full wait. In the smoke run, about 4 s after load, the base's cards showed their pictures and r3's were still empty. While the pane redraws continuously (play, a held orbit), new formulas' cards stay empty. The wait does keep stalls off the pane; this is only time to first card picture.
evidence: review-speed-runs/plog.json, All sheets: landTF, landNrm, land and landEdgeS are first used at 3085 to 3201 ms after the open, after a 1.5 s wait for the pane to go idle. review-speed-runs/cards-blank-r3-allsheets.png (r3, cards f1 and f2 empty) against cards-drawn-base-allsheets.png (base, the same moment, both drawn).
fix: Cut the idle wait to a few hundred ms, or let the cards start compiling when the pane's sheets have settled and draw once the cards' programs have settled. Cap the wait while the pane keeps drawing, for example at 3 s, so cards still appear during a long play.

title: Passed: context loss and restore, the default mesh with All sheets, playing at Max with All sheets
detail: Losing and restoring the context (WEBGL_lose_context) at rest with All sheets brings the picture back in 122 ms (base 98), pixel-identical, with the sheets' refinement rebuilt (16 032 evaluations, 25 entries) and no console errors. Losing it while playing, then restoring, gives 60 fps (p95 18.4) afterwards, and the picture after closing the deformation equals the one before. The default mesh with All sheets: 60 fps orbiting, playing and after stopping, desktop and phone, 2 runs each. One phone play run had p95 22.8 and a 55.8 ms frame; the other had p95 18.4. Playing at Max with All sheets is better than the base: r3 54.8 to 60 fps, base 50.6 to 54.4 fps, which fails BUDGET60.
